title: The Fall of the House of Usher
focus: a family and a house collapsing together

teacherSummary.text: The narrator answers a letter from his boyhood friend Roderick Usher and visits the gloomy Usher mansion, which has a faint crack running down its front. Roderick suffers from acute senses and dread; his twin Madeline wastes away and is entombed in a vault, apparently dead. Days later, during a storm, she bursts out of her tomb and falls dead on her brother, who dies of terror. The narrator flees as the house splits along the crack and sinks into the tarn.

Then start your writing prompt at your assigned level (HS Sophomore: Analyze how The Fall of the House of Usher develops the idea of a family and a house collapsing together. Make a precise claim, support it with at least three pieces of textual evidence, and explain how the author's use of setting and imagery shapes that idea. Address one possible counterclaim.) Exemplar: Poe uses the house as a mirror of Roderick's mind, so its collapse completes his. When the text says “a barely perceptible fissure, which, extending from the roof of the building in front, made its way down the wall in a zigzag direction” (The Fall of the House of Usher, paragraph 8), it shows this directly. The narrator notices "a barely perceptible fissure" from roof to ground, and Roderick foresees the day he "must abandon life and reason together"; at the end the fissure widens and house and mind fall at once.
